newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar Airways to upgrade services, get new plane.
newsitem.headline: Qatar Airways to upgrade services, get new plane.

text.p: Privately-owned Qatar Airways said on Monday a leased Airbus aircraft would join the fleet by the end of the month, raising to six the number of aircraft it operates.
The airline said it would also introduce a new corporate image and livery in the next few weeks.
"An Airbus A300-600 is due to arrive in the fourth week of this month, which will increase our fleet to two widebodied Airbuses and four Boeing 727s," a spokesman told Reuters.

The latest addition is one of two A300s leased from Australia's Ansett Worldwide, for $18 million for five years. The first joined Qatar Airways' fleet in March and is operating on the Doha-London Heathrow sector.
Both aircraft were made in 1993 and can seat 238 passengers.
"These will significantly help us to intensify and expand our operations," the spokesman said.
The airline plans to introduce a daily flight from London Heathrow to Doha from May 15, instead of the current four flights a week.
Also underway are more frequencies to the Indian subcontinent -- Bombay, Trivandrum, Karachi, Kathmandu and Dhaka -- which provides a major chunk of the airline's earnings.
He said there were plans to increase services to Bangkok, Manila, Cairo, Khartoum and Beirut.
The airline, which last week got approval for a 70 million riyal ($19.2 million) loan from the government, had set aside $2.5 million for the new corporate image and livery, the spokesman said.
